focus.jnote: The week opens risk-on — but there’s exactly one thing to verify, not a table to pound. S&P 500 futures advanced ~0.4–0.6% and Nasdaq 100 contracts ~0.6–0.8% as technology led gains across regions, and Treasuries climbed across the curve. The biggest driver: Brent crude fell for a fourth straight day, its longest such streak in three months, with WTI opening near ~$96.75 after closing above $100 Friday as Strait-of-Hormuz shipping traffic recovered. The VIX is near ~14.9, close to a year-to-date low, and the 10Y sits ~4.94%. The macro backdrop is soft (August factory output slipped 0.3%), and the big event is the Trump–Xi summit Sept 23–25 — chips, rare earths and tariffs are all on the table. The scanner boarded a single Type B name (AMD); on a calm-but-event-driven tape, verify it hard before assuming there’s a trade.

notdown: Chips & AI (SMH, NVDA, AMD, INTC) are the group with a clear bid — Nvidia, AMD and Intel all rose Monday on fresh company developments and improving sentiment, and China/Hong Kong tech rallied ahead of the summit. But be honest: much of that bid is summit-anticipation — eased chip-export rules would lift NVDA/AMD/INTC, while tighter controls trigger a supply-chain sell-off. AMD is the one name that cleared the scanner, but its catalyst reads like broad sector momentum, not a durable single-name re-rate. Watch-only outside the one boarded name.
notup: Rate-sensitive & fuel-sensitive names have less to fear today with oil falling and yields easing slightly, so clean bear-call setups are thin. Selling bear calls into a risk-on, VIX-near-lows relief tape carries squeeze risk on any continuation or a positive summit headline. The disciplined answer on the short side is to sell nothing new today.
why: Why not GREEN? Two reasons. First, even though composite (44) and P(≥1% gap) (30%) both sit below their triggers, the tape faces a live, unscheduled-style event risk in the Trump–Xi summit (Sept 23–25) that can gap chips — the exact sector of the one boarded name — either way, plus an unresolved Hormuz/oil backdrop and a ~5%-area 10-year. Second, the single boarded name (AMD, Type B · Grade A) has weak confirming inputs: light 0.04x volume, a one-sided/unquoted ATM chain, unverified liquidity, and only one S/R layer. That is a half-size, verify-first candidate, not a green light. Half size, A-grade only; confirm 4-VAL and liquidity at 9:35 before any entry. Cash is a position today.

10-year near 5% — the 10Y sits ~4.94% and global bond yields have been climbing; a rate pop back through 5% hits rate-sensitive and AI/hyperscaler names hardest and would stall the relief.

AMD liquidity & 4-VAL — the one boarded name showed a one-sided/unquoted ATM chain, light 0.04x volume and only ~940 OI. Verify the spread and 4-VAL manually at 9:35; do not enter on an unconfirmed, illiquid chain.
